title: Importing members
question: Q3
take: CSV import as column-mapping table (field / sample data / import as), upserts on matching email, and auto-labels the batch 'Import <date>' so the cohort is findable afterwards.

title: Importing members
question: Q3
take: 'Enter manually | Import CSV' is a toggle inside the same Invite wizard (not a buried settings page), with a template CSV link and tag assignment for the whole batch; answers the 'batch upload existed but nobody found it' problem.

title: Importing member from CSV
question: Q3
take: Bulk import page shows the invite email preview and defaults before upload, then a 'Bulk logs' table (Pending -> Completed 2/2, input + output CSV) so a tech can verify what actually landed.

title: Mapping fields
question: Q3
take: 3-step Upload / Map fields / Review; the review screen counts new vs existing people, warnings and errors, and offers 'add these people to a new or existing segment' — i.e. import creates the cohort in one go.

title: Manage members
question: Q3
take: Group page puts Add members / Bulk upload members / Download members side by side, and separates direct vs indirect (nested) members — a model for cohorts that contain sub-groups.

title: Inviting team members
question: Q3
take: Paste comma-separated emails + optional 'Add to team' in one dialog; invitees appear immediately in the members table with '(Invited)' status and their team chip, so the roster exists before anyone accepts.

title: Creating a teammate group
question: Q3
take: Create-group form offers both a checkbox picker of existing people AND 'Download CSV template / Import CSV' inline — small groups by hand, big cohorts by file, same screen.

title: Creating a group
question: Q3
take: People settings use Members / Guests / Groups tabs; a group is an expandable row with inline 'Add members', and the members table shows each person's teamspaces and groups — cohort membership is visible from both sides.

title: Invite members dialog (link, email, 'Import list' nudge)
question: Q3
take: Invite dialog surfaces bulk import as a one-line nudge under the email box ('Want to add emails in bulk? Import list') plus a domain-restricted join link — discoverability of bulk without a separate feature.

title: Invite teammates (link, Google/Slack contacts, emails)
question: Q3
take: Three entry paths stacked on one card: join link, pull from Google/Slack contacts, or type emails — a join link/code is the cheapest answer to a cohort that churns until week one (learners self-enrol).

title: Event registrants list with 'Sync from email list' and 'Upload CSV'
question: Q3
take: Roster header offers 'Sync from email list' next to 'Upload CSV' with an in-page progress toast; sync (continuous, from a source of truth) and upload (one-off) are distinct verbs, matching SIS/Canvas vs spreadsheet.

title: Uploading a CSV (bulk edit of workers)
question: Q3
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: download-edit-upload-validate-choose-review, a 4-stage wizard in a full-screen takeover; right for 300 payroll records, far too heavy for a sim tech adding a 4-10 learner group.

title: Changing a member role
question: Q4
take: The floor: exactly two roles (Admin / Member), each with a one-line description in the dropdown, 'Remove from workspace' as the third option; role changes are a single click with a toast, no confirm.

title: Invite member with Guest / Member / Admin / Owner dropdown
question: Q4
take: The canonical 4-role ladder with descriptions inline at invite time: Guest 'only projects they're invited to', Member 'create and access projects', Admin 'manage members and settings', Owner 'billing and transfer'.

title: Changing a role
question: Q4
take: Users page is split into Invited / Guests / Members sections; a role cell offers 'Convert to guest' / 'Convert to admin' / 'Remove' with a lightweight inline confirm — guest is a conversion, not a separate account type.

title: Editing member role
question: Q4
take: Three roles (Employee / Auditor / Admin) as a segmented control with the selected role's description underneath; members table also has 'Import from spreadsheet' and a join link right in the header.

title: Inviting people (guest)
question: Q4
take: Switching 'Invite as' to Guest progressively reveals required channels + an expiration date; a guest is scoped to content and time — the pattern for simulated patients or visiting faculty without a dedicated global role.

title: Downgrading a member
question: Q4
take: Member -> Guest downgrade opens a confirm that spells out the consequences ('can only access channels they've been invited to, can't invite members') with an explicit 'Yes, I'm absolutely sure' checkbox.

title: Inviting a guest
question: Q4
take: Per-item escape hatch on top of workspace roles: Share panel lists people (with 'Guest' badge), the teamspace, and 'General access: Everyone at <workspace>', each with its own Full access / Can edit / Can comment level.

title: Updating sharing permissions
question: Q4
take: Share dialog stacks audience rows — anyone with link / anyone in workspace / inherited from folder (greyed) / named people — each with Can view / comment / edit / No access; inherited rows are shown but locked.

title: Share space with 'Inherited' org access and explicit per-person role
question: Q4
take: Labels the org-wide row as 'Inherited' with member count while a named person has an explicit 'Administrator' override, plus a toggle to mint a guest link with its own role — three layers, one small panel.

title: Share a document
question: Q4
take: Share dialog is tabbed by audience — Workspace Members (Restricted) / Guests / Everyone (No Access) — with the current state in the tab label; a clean mental model for 'who can see this scenario'.

title: Adding a new role
question: Q4
take: Roles as cards with plain-language descriptions and head counts, plus a dashed 'Add new role' card as the escape hatch; custom role permissions are grouped by AREA with just View / Edit columns, not per-action toggles.

title: Adding a role
question: Q4
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: roles x permissions checkbox matrix that gains a column per role and a row per action; adding 'Contributor' means auditing ~30 cells. This is what 8 global roles turns into.

title: Team permissions matrix (Basic / Low / Med / High / Owner)
question: Q4
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: permission levels named Basic/Low/Med/High carry no meaning — the admin must read the whole grid to know what 'Med' does; role names should describe a job, not a rank.
